title: fix: attribute text errors to the actual upstream
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Preserve provider URL and status so alerts identify the actual upstream instead of `gen.pollinations.ai`.
- Pass provider `429` responses through as `RATE_LIMITED`; transport/parsing failures remain `502`, while Pollinations processing bugs remain `500`.
- Remove internal `cause` data from public error responses and preserve fallback metadata during response serialization.

Why: text error handling discarded upstream context, substituted the incoming Gen URL, and classified provider rate limits as server failures.

Checks:
- Biome and Gen typecheck passed
- 19 Gen/shared/docs suites, 201 tests passed
- Enter typecheck passed
- Enter runtime tests were not run because their mandatory pretest writes decrypted secrets to `.dev.vars`

gist.headline: Errors find their real home
gist.blurb: The text gateway now keeps the upstream’s address on the envelope. Provider rate limits are recognized as rate limits, while public errors leave the internal wiring in the hive.
gist.summary: Text-generation error handling now preserves the originating provider URL and status, returns upstream 429s as RATE_LIMITED, keeps transport and parsing failures at 502, and reserves 500 for Pollinations processing errors.
gist.impact: Developers and alerts can now identify the actual upstream behind a failed text request, while API clients receive clearer rate-limit and failure classifications without internal cause data.
gist.visual_concept: Polli acts as a careful mail carrier in a cozy code garden, attaching clear provider-address labels to error-message envelopes instead of sending everything to the Gen mailbox. A friendly CRT monitor robot sorts envelopes into clearly marked 429, 502, and 500 baskets beside flowering code-plants, representing accurate attribution and classification.
